This vignette shows the functions for summarising and plotting time-to-event
outcomes in a two-arm trial:

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sstable.survcomp()` | events, risk, median time and the arm comparison (Cox, Fine-Gray, RMST or cumulative incidence) |
| `sstable.survcomp.subgroup()` | the same comparison within subgroups, with a heterogeneity test |
| `rbind()` | stacks two comparison tables (e.g. two populations) |
| `gg_ajsurvplot()`, `gg_ajsurvplot2()` | Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence curves for competing risks |
| `ggsurvfit2()`, `tidy_survfit2()` | Kaplan-Meier curves and tidy data that keep each stratifying variable as a column |

```{r}
library(C306)
library(survival)
```

## Example data

The package ships `baseline_data`, a **simulated** two-arm trial in tetanus
(271 participants). It has no follow-up times, so for illustration we derive a
time-to-event outcome from the days spent in the intensive care unit
(`icudays`): each participant leaves the ICU either alive (discharge) or by
death (`outcome == 4`), and follow-up is censored at day 28.

```{r}
icu <- subset(baseline_data, !is.na(icudays))
icu$Arm <- factor(icu$Arm, levels = c("Sham procedure", "Intrathecal treatment"))
icu$time <- pmin(icu$icudays, 28)
icu$event <- factor(
  ifelse(icu$icudays > 28, "censor", ifelse(icu$outcome == 4, "death", "discharge")),
  levels = c("censor", "discharge", "death")
)
table(icu$Arm, icu$event)
```

The first level of `event` is the censoring code, as `survival::Surv()`
expects for competing-risks data. Because the data are simulated, the numbers
below illustrate the functions and say nothing about the treatment.

## Comparing two arms: `sstable.survcomp()`

The arm must be the first covariate on the right-hand side of the model. With
the default `compare.method = "cox"`, the table shows, for each arm, the number
of events out of the number of participants with the event probability at the
end of follow-up, the hazard ratio with its 95% CI and p-value, a test for
proportional hazards and the median (IQR) time to event.

Here the event is discharge alive, and deaths are censored (a cause-specific
analysis):

```{r}
sstable.survcomp(Surv(time, event == "discharge") ~ Arm, data = icu)
```

By default the output is a `flextable`. Use `flextable = FALSE` to get the
underlying character matrix and footer, which you can edit or combine:

```{r}
tab <- sstable.survcomp(Surv(time, event == "discharge") ~ Arm, data = icu,
                        flextable = FALSE)
tab$table
tab$footer
```

Other covariates can be added after the arm; the comparison is then adjusted
for them:

```{r}
sstable.survcomp(Surv(time, event == "discharge") ~ Arm + age + sex, data = icu)
```

### Restricted mean survival time

`compare.method = "rmst"` compares the restricted mean time to event up to
`time` instead of the hazard. Here it is the mean number of days in the ICU,
restricted to the first 28 days:

```{r}
sstable.survcomp(Surv(time, event != "censor") ~ Arm, data = icu, time = 28,
                 compare.method = "rmst")
```

`compare.args = list(type = "ratio")` gives a ratio instead of a difference.
`compare.method = "cuminc"` compares the cumulative incidence at `time` in the
same way.

### Competing risks

When the left-hand side has a factor event, `sstable.survcomp()` fits a
Fine-Gray model for the cause named in `compare.args` and reports the
Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence. Here death competes with discharge:

```{r}
sstable.survcomp(Surv(time, event) ~ Arm, data = icu,
                 compare.args = list(cause = "discharge"))
```

## Subgroups: `sstable.survcomp.subgroup()`

Give the base model and a one-sided formula with the subgroup variable. The
table shows the comparison overall and within each subgroup, with a test for
the arm-by-subgroup interaction:

```{r}
icu$ablett <- factor(icu$ablettscore, levels = c("I", "II", "III"),
                     labels = c("Ablett I", "Ablett II", "Ablett III"))
sstable.survcomp.subgroup(Surv(time, event == "discharge") ~ Arm, ~ ablett,
                          data = icu)
```

It accepts the same `compare.method` and `compare.args` as
`sstable.survcomp()`.

## Stacking tables: `rbind()`

Tables made with `flextable = FALSE` can be stacked, for example to show the
whole population and a sub-population in one table. The header of the first
table is kept:

```{r}
all_pts <- sstable.survcomp(Surv(time, event == "discharge") ~ Arm, data = icu,
                            medsum = FALSE, flextable = FALSE)
no_vaso <- sstable.survcomp(Surv(time, event == "discharge") ~ Arm,
                            data = subset(icu, vaso == "N"),
                            medsum = FALSE, flextable = FALSE)
both <- rbind(all_pts, no_vaso)
ss_flextable(both)
```

## Cumulative incidence curves

`gg_ajsurvplot()` takes the same formula as `survival::survfit()` and draws
the Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence of one event type (`etype`):

```{r}
gg_ajsurvplot(Surv(time, event) ~ Arm, data = icu, etype = "discharge",
              fun = "event")
```

`gg_ajsurvplot2()` draws the main event and the competing event together, one
panel per arm by default (`facet.by = ~ strata`):

```{r}
gg_ajsurvplot2(Surv(time, event) ~ Arm, data = icu,
               main.event = "discharge", competing.event = "death")
```

Both return `ggplot` objects, so they can be modified with the usual `ggplot2`
functions.

## Kaplan-Meier curves with several strata

`ggsurvfit::ggsurvfit()` merges all stratifying variables into one `strata`
column. `ggsurvfit2()` keeps each variable as its own column, so you can facet
by one variable and colour by another:

```{r}
fit <- survfit(Surv(time, event == "discharge") ~ Arm + sex, data = icu)
ggsurvfit2(fit, type = "risk") + ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ sex)
```

`tidy_survfit2()` returns the same data as a data frame, one column per
stratifying variable:

```{r}
head(tidy_survfit2(fit, times = c(7, 14, 21, 28)))
```
